items.title: 6.11.1 Entropy, diffusion and the number of ways of arrangement

blocks.text: We can show that the molecules in a vapour diffuse by chance by thinking about the probability of finding them at one place at any one time. Consider the simplified model shown in Figure 6.10 below.

blocks.alt: Two horizontal gas jars joined end to end with a partition between them. Gas jar A on the left holds three molecules numbered 1, 2 and 3; gas jar B on the right is empty. Labels: partition, gas jar A, gas jar B.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.10: Diffusion and number of possible arrangements (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.10).

blocks.text: There are 8 different ways for these molecules to arrange themselves in two jars by diffusion from Jar A to jar B. that is

Similarly, if there were 5 molecules initially in jar A, the possible ways of arrangement will be 2⁵, i.e. 32. And if there were 100 molecules, the probability will be 2¹⁰⁰. A general formula xʸ can be written for the calculation of probability, where x is the number of places and y is the number of particles to be arranged.

Diffusion happens because there is a large number of ways of arranging the molecules. The concept of the ‘number of ways’ of arrangement either particles or the energy within these particles helps predict whether it can happen or not.
